name: Autoimmune Polyglandular Syndrome Type 2 with Gastrointestinal Manifestations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Autoimmune Polyglandular Syndrome Type 2

criteria.description: Presence of primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease)
Coexisting autoimmune thyroid disease (Hashimoto thyroiditis or Graves disease)
Evidence of autoimmune gastritis or pernicious anemia
Detection of relevant autoantibodies (e.g., 21-hydroxylase, thyroid peroxidase, intrinsic factor antibodies)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of primary adrenal insufficiency plus autoimmune thyroid disease, with or without type 1 diabetes mellitus
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Gastrointestinal manifestations such as autoimmune gastritis and malabsorption support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Primary adrenal insufficiency symptoms (fatigue, hypotension, hyperpigmentation)
Autoimmune thyroid disease symptoms (goiter, hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism signs)

pathognomonic.notes: Includes vitamin B12 deficiency and macrocytic anemia

common.symptomName: Type 1 diabetes mellitus symptoms (polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss)

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms related to B12 deficiency (paresthesia, ataxia)

rare.notes: Considered rare but reported in some cases

laboratory: Elevated ACTH with low cortisol (primary adrenal insufficiency)
Positive thyroid peroxidase and thyroglobulin antibodies
Macrocytic anemia with low vitamin B12
imaging: Adrenal gland atrophy on CT or MRI
Thyroid ultrasound showing autoimmune thyroiditis features
other: Histopathology of gastric mucosa showing lymphocytic infiltration and glandular atrophy

distinguishingFeatures: Villous atrophy on small bowel biopsy

redFlags: Acute adrenal crisis (hypotension, shock, electrolyte imbalance)
Severe malabsorption with weight loss and nutritional deficiencies
Neurological deficits due to untreated pernicious anemia
references: Betterle C, Dal Pra C, Mantero F, Zanchetta R. Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 2. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 1998;83(4):1049-1055.
Nishikawa T, et al. Autoimmune gastritis and pernicious anemia in autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 2. Autoimmunity Reviews. 2014;13(4-5): 414-419.
Neufeld M, Maclaren NK. Autoimmune polyglandular syndromes. Pediatr Ann. 1987;16(9): 554-559.
